title: Fourier expansion of noise stability
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$. Choose $x$ uniformly from the sign cube, then obtain $y$ by independently keeping each coordinate of $x$ with probability $(1+\rho)/2$ and flipping it otherwise. The expected product $\mathbb E[f(x)f(y)]$ equals $\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{n}\rho^k\sum_{\ egin{subarray}{c}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\\|S|=k\end{subarray}}\widehat f(S)^2$, where $\widehat f(S)=\mathbb E_x\!\left[f(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i\right]$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-coordinate sign cube
